headline: calibrated

population.source: USDA Crop Sequence Boundaries (2016-2023 polygons), Maryland, checked against the 2025 Cropland Data Layer
population.corn_rule: CSB field with at least 50% of its 30 m CDL 2025 pixel centres in class 1 (Corn)

model.name: Logistic regression on NDVI and harvest-timing features (L1), model v2
model.description: model v2 (pre-registered candidate H, baseline/model_v2): median imputation, standard scaling, L1 logistic regression (liblinear) with C chosen by field-grouped inner CV, threshold 0.5

calibrated.method: share = (q - FPR) / (TPR - FPR), clipped to [0, 1]; q is the acre share of scored sample fields called Silage at 0.5; TPR and FPR are acre-weighted rates from the 44 saved held-out BARC field-years

nass_2025.source: USDA NASS Quick Stats, 2025 survey, acres harvested (data/reference/quickstats_2025_judges.csv)

method: Maryland 2025 corn fields are Crop Sequence Boundaries polygons with at least half of their 2025 Cropland Data Layer pixels in corn: 18,684 fields, 442,169 acres. A seeded random sample of 1,500 fields, allocated by county, was read from Sentinel-2 L2A (July-November 2025) with the baseline's cloud mask and reflectance offset, giving nine NDVI features and four harvest-timing features per field. Model v2 (L1 logistic regression), fitted on all 44 labeled BARC field-years, gives each field a silage probability. Raw: probability-weighted silage acres in the sample, scaled to all Maryland corn acres. Calibrated: the acre share called silage, corrected with the miss and false-alarm rates measured on held-out BARC fields. Grain is corn acres minus silage. The 2025 NASS values were not used to fit, choose or adjust anything.
limitations: The model was trained on 44 field-years from one research farm (BARC, 2021-2023); how well it transfers to other Maryland farms and to 2025 is untested.
The calibration rates come from 12 silage and 32 grain BARC field-years, so the calibrated range is wide.
The raw range reflects only which fields were sampled, not model error, so it is too narrow.
Field polygons date from 2023; corn in 2025 is taken from the Cropland Data Layer, which has its own classification error.
Corn acres here are mapped field acres, not NASS acres harvested; abandoned or failed corn is not removed.
Fields with fewer than 3 clear Sentinel-2 dates are skipped and listed, not filled in.

The timing feature drop_size is the largest NDVI fall between consecutive clear looks, so it grows with the gap between looks. BARC fields share scenes and cloud gaps; the statewide sample does not. Days between clear looks: 2025 sample median 5, 90th percentile 15, median longest gap per field 23; BARC training median 5, 90th percentile 15, median longest gap 29.

Model v2 was chosen on BARC held-out data (selection-corrected balanced accuracy about 0.87 vs 0.80 for v1; the bootstrap interval for the gain touches zero); its timing features are untested outside BARC.
